text:
maria: noticing a pretty sharp token/sec sag on canary after yesterday's runtime merge. baseline tok/sec ~120k, canary dropped to ~56k during warmup for 1-2m then recovered. linking profile and sample logs. :eyes:
kevin: ugh, saw alerts this morning. is this the kernel-selection change (auto-fallback heuristics) that went in?
olga: maybe related to the new early-prefetch path — it changes the kernel hint set on startup. I saw memcopy counts spike in the flamegraph.
raj: quick numbers from perf-run against same model:
```
2026-03-17T09:02:11Z start warmup
epoch 0: tok/sec 54k, mean latency 320ms
epoch 1: tok/sec 118k, mean latency 110ms
kv-cache hitrate: 7% -> 72% after warmup
kernel chosen: fallback_int8_memcopy (lots of memcpy)
```
maria: exact. kv-cache warmup prolonged — lots of tiny batches (size 1-2) for first ~30s. scheduler seems to be preempting coalescer and routing to fallback kernels that incur a big memcopy.
kevin: can you paste the kernel-selection log snippet?
maria: here — it's noisy but shows multiple re-routes in a short window:
```
[09:02:12.342] route_request -> kernel_hint { preferred: fp16, fallback: int8_memcopy }
[09:02:12.343] allocate_batch -> size=1
[09:02:12.344] schedule -> selected_kernel=int8_memcopy
[09:02:12.345] post_exec -> memcpy_bytes=12.4MB
[09:02:13.121] kvcache miss -> insert prefix
[09:02:13.122] coalesce_wake -> batch_size=3
[09:02:13.123] selected_kernel=fp16_fastpath
```
olga: that pattern explains the memcopy spike and token/sec dip. repeated int8 fallback then fp16 fastpath churn during warmup kills throughput.
raj: possible root causes: 1) heuristic threshold for hinting too conservative on cold KV cache, 2) scheduler wake timing produces many size-1 batches, 3) an unintended priority preemption bug after the merge.
kevin: CI perf run did not fail, probably because our synthetic load hits different seq distribution vs. canary. Need a reproduce-case in CI where warmup KV cache is cold and inter-arrival jitter matches canary.
ci-bot: deploy status: canary v3.7.4 -> 30% traffic. no automated revert. :warning:
maria: immediate mitigation options: pin kernel hint to fp16_fastpath for canary (config override), throttle preemption for first 45s of instance startup, or temporarily revert the early-prefetch change.
olga: config override is fastest. I can push a canary patch to force hint preference, test now?
kevin: +1 do that and monitor tok/sec and memcopy metrics. if we see recovery, promote and schedule revert PR to investigate heuristics.
raj: I'll start a short bisect on the merge — especially the scheduler preempt change and the prefetch PRs. I can run a targeted perf job that reproduces the warmup dip.
maria: thanks. pushing a config patch now. patch: `canary.kernel.hint_override=fp16_fastpath`
olga: patch applied to canary nodes. watching dashboards. :eyes:
(20s later)
olga: tok/sec jumped back to 116k within 30s, memcpy spikes disappeared. kv-cache hitrate warmed as expected.
kevin: great. keep the override until we have a real fix. also add a regression CI test that replicates cold-kv + jitter.
raj: bisect result preliminary: the scheduler preempt change + reduced coalescer patience combined to cause undercoalescing during warmup. candidate PR 4521.
maria: filing a rollback follow-up: revert PR 4521 for now, leave prefetch in but increase coalescer patience. I'll open the revert PR and link the perf traces.
kevin: assign to eng-runtime and add to next standup. thanks all. :thumbsup:
